subject: Risk & Compliance
title: Credit Default Swaps
description: A 1-minute de-risking session on Credit Default Swaps.

hook.text: A bank lends money and worries the borrower defaults. So it buys protection from a third party.

buildup.text: Credit default swaps transfer default risk to others. The CDS market exploded in the 2000s.

discovery.text: By 2008, the CDS market topped sixty trillion dollars — larger than the entire world's GDP.

twist.text: When Lehman collapsed, the web of CDS contracts nearly brought down the global financial system.

climax.text: A tool for reducing risk created hidden chains that amplified it catastrophically.

punchline.text: Risk transferred isn't risk eliminated. It's hidden.

quiz.question: What went wrong with credit default swaps in 2008?
options: They were too expensive to buy
